key_insight: CBTV preserves particle identities in dense granular flows by tracking coloured neighbour constellations before linking individual particles.
engineering_relevance: For experiments with coloured grains, CBTV can ease ultra-high-frame-rate requirements when particles move roughly half to twice their spacing between frames.
method: Use cross-correlation to estimate a motion prior.
Match neighbouring coloured particles as constellations.
Assign remaining particles individually in a training-free, multi-pass workflow.
evidence_signal: Evaluation against 12 baseline tracker configurations on 59 cases from 15 simulated granular flows with exact ground truth found CBTV matched or exceeded every baseline on impulsive collisions at all tested displacements.
watch_item: Beyond roughly 2–3 particle diameters per frame, CBTV's motion prior becomes limiting, and bulk-motion-compensating trackers are more accurate.
paper_title: CBTV: Colour Bean Tracking Velocimetry for Dense Granular Flows
